steps.message:
The bug is fixed. Here's a summary of what I found and changed.

## Diagnosis

Reproduced the crash with a Robolectric test:

```
java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index: 1, Size: 1
  at com.ichi2.anki.CardBrowser.hasSelectedSingleNoteId(CardBrowser.java:392)
  at com.ichi2.anki.CardBrowser.updateMultiselectMenu(...)
  at com.ichi2.anki.CardBrowser.onSelectionChanged(...)
  at com.ichi2.anki.CardBrowser.updateList(...)   ← from the search-cards task result
```

Root cause: `CardBrowser` stores the multi-select selection as **list positions** (`mCheckedCardPositions`), not card ids. When the note type is changed in the `NoteEditor`, it returns `reloadRequired`, so the browser throws away its card list and re-runs the search. `Models.change()` deletes the cards that map to nothing (e.g. 2-template type → 1-template type), so the new list is shorter, while the stale positions are still selected. Every subsequent access (`hasSelectedSingleNoteId()`, `getSelectedCardIds()`, `getCheckedCardIds()`, and the background `TASK_TYPE_CHECK_CARD_SELECTION`) then indexes past the end of the list and crashes — exactly the "multi-select → Edit → change card type" scenario in the report.

## Fix

`AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/anki/CardBrowser.java`
- Remember the **card ids** of the selection before a search clears the list (`mCheckedCardIdsBeforeSearch`).
- New `restoreSelectionAfterSearch()`, called when search results arrive: re-maps the selected ids to their new positions, drops cards that no longer exist, and leaves multi-select mode if nothing selected remains.
- Made `getSelectedCardIds()`, `hasSelectedSingleNoteId()` and `getCheckedCardIds()` bounds-safe, so stale positions are skipped rather than throwing while a reload is in flight.
- `endMultiSelectMode()` / `onSelectNone()` also discard remembered ids so an in-flight search can't resurrect a cleared selection.

`AnkiDroid/src/main/java/com/ichi2/async/CollectionTask.java`
- `doInBackgroundCheckCardSelection()`: iterate over a copy of the positions, skip out-of-range positions, and tolerate cards deleted in the meantime (this ran on a background thread, so it crashed the app outright).

`AnkiDroid/src/test/java/com/ichi2/anki/CardBrowserTest.java`
- Added regression test `changingNoteTypeInMultiSelectModeDoesNotCrash()` which selects both cards of a note, performs the note-type change that removes a card, and asserts the browser survives with a correctly-pruned selection (this test fails with the original code).

Verification: `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` succeeds, and the whole unit test suite (`:AnkiDroid:testDebugUnitTest`) passes.
